page.overview:
Who is Black Buddha?

The Black Buddha is an avatar of Nyarlathotep who first appeared in Masayuki Shuno's 2001 novel Kuroi Hotoke.

According to legend, the Black Buddha statue washed ashore at Akuhama in 877 CE, having been part of the cargo of a ship that sank at sea. Its survival was taken as a sign of divine favor, and a Buddhist monk later built a temple around it, which came to be known as Anranji. There, the figure was worshipped as the bodhisattva Kurochier Kanzeon, or simply Kuromi-sama.

Over time, the statue came to be associated with a series of unsettling and supernatural events said to have plagued Anranji for centuries, as well as with Japan's Tendai Buddhist sect.

In the novel, Detective Isurugi was hired to locate a Tang dynasty treasure linked to the 9th-century Tendai monk Enzai, believed to have been lost in a shipwreck. His investigation leads him to Anranji, where Kuromi-sama is venerated, and the case soon takes a darker turn with the discovery of an unidentified corpse. As the mystery unfolds, it is revealed that the Black Buddha is in fact an avatar of Nyarlathotep, whose hidden influence lies behind the temple's long history of inexplicable horrors. (: Kuroi Hotoke)
